parts.text:
The lighthouse had stood on Cormorant Point for eighty years, and Edda had kept it for thirty of them. Each night she climbed the spiral stairs, lit the lamp, and watched its beam sweep the dark water like a slow, patient hand.

She never married. The sea had asked for all of her, and she'd given it gladly. Sailors she'd never meet owed her their lives, though most never knew her name.

One October night, static crackled through her radio: a fishing boat, engine dead, drifting toward the rocks. Edda didn't call for help—there wasn't time. She lit a signal fire on the point itself, waving it like a beacon until the boat's captain saw the flames and steered hard away.

At dawn, the boat radioed its thanks to "the lighthouse." Edda smiled, extinguished her fire, and climbed back up to sleep. The sea had asked, and she had answered, as always.
